summary: Same utility concept and identical mode/control structure (uniform whole-rig colour-temperature field, auto-sweep below slider ~0.067, static above), but the port's slider-to-colour mapping is compressed to roughly the middle 40% of the original's temperature range and its auto sweep runs 2.1x too slow.
observations: Control surface matches exactly: both sides expose one control, sliderColorTemperature (kind slider, label ColorTemperature). No missing/extra/renamed dials.

Both sides render a SPATIALLY UNIFORM solid colour on every frame - every pixel identical. Confirmed by --dump on the default 60 px strip, on --pixels 300, and on --rig grid --grid 16x16: all three rigs give the same single colour per side per time, so both sides are rig- and index-independent. Both are seed-independent (seed 1 vs 1234 byte-identical).

Both sides have the SAME two-regime structure with the SAME boundary: slider <= 0.065 (and untouched, which the probe confirms is byte-identical to slider=0) gives an animated temperature sweep; slider >= 0.070 gives a static solid colour (motion 0 over a 30 s window on both sides). Boundary bracketed to (0.065, 0.070] on BOTH sides - a genuine structural match.

AUTO-MODE PERIOD DIVERGENCE: autocorrelation of meanB gives orig 92 frames @20fps = 4.60 s and 183 frames @40fps = 4.58 s; port 192 frames @20fps = 9.60 s and 384 frames @40fps = 9.60 s. Both sides are fps-invariant (time-based, not frame-stepped) - the port is simply ~2.09x slower.

AUTO-MODE RANGE DIVERGENCE: the original's sweep reaches pure red (255,0,0) and HOLDS there ~0.4 s per cycle (t=3.2-3.5 s), and holds at its cool extreme (201,209,255) (t=1.0-1.2 s) - i.e. it clips/plateaus at both ends. The port never clips: it turns around smoothly at (255,70,0) warm and (221,230,255) cool, so its swing is visibly less extreme at both ends and has no dwell.

STATIC-MODE MAPPING DIVERGENCE (the headline): at the same dial setting the two sides render clearly different colours. slider 0.07: orig (255,0,0) pure red vs port (255,135,11) light orange. slider 0.1: orig (255,37,0) vs port (255,155,60). slider 0.2: orig (255,131,41) vs port (255,200,156). slider 0.4: orig (255,225,211) warm cream vs port (255,255,252) pure white. slider 0.7: orig (158,177,255) vs port (196,215,255). slider 1.0: orig (115,144,255) deep blue vs port (181,205,255) pale blue.

Projecting each port colour onto the original's own curve: the port's ENTIRE slider travel 0.07..1.00 reproduces only orig 0.18..0.58. The compression is strongly nonlinear at the cool end - port 0.40->1.00 (60% of the slider) covers only orig 0.44->0.58 (14% of the original's travel), so the top half of the port's dial is nearly dead visually while the original is still deepening from cream to saturated blue.

Numerically the port's static curve looks like a LINEAR ~2000K..15000K blackbody ramp (port 0.25 = (255,217,187) vs the standard 4500K (255,219,186); port 1.0 = (255->181,205,255) which is exactly the standard 15000K entry). The original's curve is far wider and non-linear in the same units (~<1000K at slider 0.07 up to well past 20000K at slider 1.0, roughly geometric in temperature), and at the cool end it leaves the blackbody locus entirely (orig 0.6 = (181,194,255), bluer than any blackbody value with that red level).

Secondary chromaticity offset: even after reparameterising, the port's cool half sits ~7-9 RGB units off the original's locus (consistently a few counts greener / less blue at the same red level), and the neutral point differs - the original's whitest static colour is a slightly pink (245,227,231) around slider 0.42, the port passes through a true (255,255,252) around slider 0.40.

Neither side is dead or degenerate: orig mean brightness 173 / motion 16.4 and port 202 / 6.7 over the 60 s survey, brightnessTrend steady on both, no compile or runtime errors, wantsSensors false on both.
Direction of the mapping agrees on both sides: increasing slider = warmer -> white -> cooler; untouched default is auto-sweep mode on both.

dials.name: sliderColorTemperature
dials.origEffect: Below ~0.067 (including untouched) puts the pattern into an auto sweep: whole rig cycles warm<->cool with a 4.60 s period, clipping/holding at pure red (255,0,0) and at (201,209,255). At >=0.07 it freezes to a static uniform colour selected by the dial, spanning pure red (255,0,0) at 0.07 through a slightly pink white ~(245,227,231) near 0.42 to deep blue (115,144,255) at 1.0 - a wide, non-linear temperature ramp.
dials.portEffect: Same two regimes with the same ~0.067 boundary and the same warm->white->cool direction, but the auto sweep has a 9.60 s period (2.09x slow) and never reaches the extremes (turnaround at (255,70,0) and (221,230,255), no dwell). Static mode spans only (255,135,11) at 0.07 through true white ~(255,255,252) near 0.40 to pale blue (181,205,255) at 1.0 - roughly a linear 2000K..15000K ramp, i.e. only the middle ~40% of the original's range, with the top 60% of the dial producing almost no further change.

feedback: Widen the static temperature range at BOTH ends. At slider 0.07 the original renders pure red (255,0,0); the port renders (255,135,11), a light orange that is roughly the original's slider-0.18 colour. At slider 1.0 the original renders deep blue (115,144,255); the port renders pale blue (181,205,255), roughly the original's slider-0.58 colour. The port's whole dial travel currently covers only orig 0.18..0.58.

The compression is worst at the cool end and is nonlinear: the port's slider 0.40->1.00 (60% of travel) reproduces only orig 0.44->0.58. A user turning the port's dial past halfway sees almost nothing change, whereas the original keeps deepening toward saturated blue. Match the original's response shape, not just its endpoints - useful checkpoints on the original's curve are 0.1=(255,37,0), 0.2=(255,131,41), 0.3=(255,186,126), 0.4=(255,225,211), 0.5=(213,216,255), 0.7=(158,177,255), 0.9=(126,153,255), 1.0=(115,144,255).

The original's cool end is NOT a standard blackbody table extrapolation - at slider 0.6 it renders (181,194,255), bluer (lower green at the same red) than the bluest blackbody entry. The port's curve tracks a textbook ~2000K..15000K blackbody table almost exactly. If the port is using a canonical Kelvin table, the original is using something with a wider/steeper cool tail; reproduce the original's curve rather than a physically-correct one.

The auto-sweep (slider <= ~0.065 or untouched) is 2.09x too slow: the original's full warm->cool->warm cycle takes 4.60 s, the port's takes 9.60 s. Both sides are already time-based (fps-invariant at 10/20/40 fps), so this is a period constant, not frame-rate coupling - halve the port's sweep period.

The original's auto sweep CLIPS at both extremes - it sits at pure red (255,0,0) for ~0.4 s and at (201,209,255) for ~0.2 s each cycle before turning around. The port glides smoothly through its turnarounds at (255,70,0) and (221,230,255) with no dwell and a narrower swing. Extend the port's sweep so it saturates and holds at the same extremes.

Everything else already matches and should not be touched: control name/kind/label, the auto-vs-static mode split and its ~0.067 threshold, the spatially-uniform whole-rig output, rig- and seed-independence, and the warm->cool dial direction.
